instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.24 Payment of minimum wages (Minnesota Fair Labor Standards Act)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage = rate set under subd. 1(c) from 2018-01-01; 90-day training wage for employees under 20 (subd. 1(b)). Indexation: by Aug 31 each year DLI determines the 12-month change in the PCE implicit price deflator (BEA); both rates rise by the lesser of 5% or that percentage, rounded to the nearest cent, never reduced, effective the next Jan 1. No tip credit: gratuities may not be applied to the minimum wage (subd. 2); tips are the employee's property, pooling only voluntary (subd. 3); card tips paid no later than the next scheduled pay period (subd. 3a). Uniform/equipment deductions capped at 50 USD and never below the minimum wage; reimbursed at termination (subd. 4-5). History ends 2024 c 110: no 2025/2026 amendment.

instrument_name: DLI page: Minimum wage in Minnesota (rates 2026 and 2027)
authority: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 11.41 USD/h from 2026-01-01 and 11.87 USD/h from 2027-01-01 (all employers); 90-day training wage (under 20) 9.31 from 2026-01-01 and 9.68 from 2027-01-01. 'No employer may take a tip credit against minimum wages in Minnesota.' Page points to the Minneapolis and St. Paul city minimum wages. Consistency check: 11.87/11.41 = 1.0403 and 9.68/9.31 = 1.0397, both under the 5% cap of 177.24 subd. 1(c); the PCE percentage itself was not read (DLI minimum-wage report not fetched).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.25 Overtime
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime at 1.5x the regular rate for hours over 48 in a workweek (state rule; FLSA 40 hours governs FLSA-covered employers). Public employers may give comp time at 1.5 h per hour over 48. Health care facilities: 14-day period by prior agreement, overtime over 8 h/day and 80 h/14 days. Exemptions: commission auto/farm-implement sales and mechanics, on-farm silo piece rate, air carrier voluntary shift trades.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.23 subd. 7 Definition of employee (MFLSA exemptions)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: MFLSA 'employee' excludes: small salaried agricultural groups (2 or fewer salaried, or salary above 48 h at minimum + 17 h at 1.5x); certain minors in agriculture and corn detasselers (for 177.24); seasonal camp staff; bona fide executive/administrative/professional and outside salespeople (<=20% of sales on premises); volunteers for nonprofits; elected officials; political-subdivision police/fire; taxicab drivers; sole-practitioner babysitters; seasonal carnival/circus/fair/ski (for 177.25 overtime only); minors under 18 working under 20 h/week in municipal recreation; DOT-regulated drivers (49 USC 31502); seafarers; clergy and members of religious orders serving under religious obligations.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.101 Wages; how often paid (as amended by Laws 2026 c 106 art 15 s 5)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: All wages (salary, earnings, gratuities) paid at least once every 31 days, commissions at least every 3 months, on a regular payday designated in advance; wages for the first half of the first 31-day period due on the first regular payday after the first day of work; wages are earned on the day worked; agricultural labor included. DLI demand: if unpaid 10 days after demand, penalty = average daily earnings per day. (b) paid on-call firefighters, first responders, volunteer ambulance: every 31 days unless mutually agreed longer. Last amended 2026 c 106 art 15 s 5 (firefighter wording only, see US-MNS5-022).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.13 Penalty for failure to pay wages promptly (discharge)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge: earned and unpaid wages and commissions immediately due on the employee's written demand; default if not paid within 24 hours after demand; penalty = average daily earnings for each day up to 15 days. Public employer needing board approval: the 24 h run from the first board meeting after discharge. Paid in the usual manner unless the employee asks for mail (postmark date = payment date).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.14 Payment to employees who quit or resign
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Resignation: wages and commissions paid in full no later than the first regularly scheduled payday after the final day (unless a CBA differs); if that payday is less than 5 calendar days after the final day, may wait until the second regular payday but no later than 20 calendar days after the final day. Migrant workers: within 3 days. Late: payable on written demand, penalty average daily earnings up to 15 days. Employees entrusted with money/property: employer has 10 calendar days to audit. No deduction for loss/indebtedness except as 181.79 permits.

instrument_name: Minneapolis Minimum Wage (City of Minneapolis Labor Standards site)
authority: City of Minneapolis, Labor Standards Enforcement Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Minneapolis minimum wage 16.37 USD/h for work performed in Minneapolis during 2026; 17.02 USD/h from 2027-01-01; same rate regardless of employer size or employee age; indexed every January 1 for inflation, capped at 5%.

instrument_name: Saint Paul Minimum Wage Ordinance rates (city HREEO Labor Standards page)
authority: City of Saint Paul, Department of Human Rights and Equal Economic Opportunity, Labor Standards
figure_or_rule_carried: Macro (10,001+ employees) and City of Saint Paul: 16.37 from 2026-01-01; Large (101-10,000): 16.37 from 2026-01-01; Small (6-100): 15.00 from 2025-07-01, 16.37 from 2026-07-01; Micro (5 or fewer): 13.25 from 2025-07-01, 14.25 from 2026-07-01, 15.00 from 2027-07-01, city indexed rate from 2028-07-01; youth/training wage 12.75 from 2025-07-01, 13.95 from 2026-07-01. Macro/Large from 2027-01-01 and Small from 2027-07-01: 'City Rate' = inflation-indexed (figure not on the page). City minimum applies from the 18th birthday even within the first 90 days. Ordinance text on Municode not fetched.

instrument_name: Minnesota Income Tax Withholding Instruction Booklet and Tax Tables 2026 (wh-inst-26): computer formula, deposits, returns, W-2
authority: Minnesota Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Formula (supersedes formulas before 2026-01-01): annualise wages (x360/52/26/24/12/1), minus allowances x 5,300. Single: 4,700-38,010 at 5.35% of excess over 4,700; 38,010-114,130 = 1,782.09 + 6.80% over 38,010; 114,130-207,850 = 6,958.25 + 7.85% over 114,130; over 207,850 = 14,315.27 + 9.85% over 207,850. Married: 14,700-63,400 at 5.35% over 14,700; 63,400-208,180 = 2,605.45 + 6.80%; 208,180-352,630 = 12,450.49 + 7.85%; over 352,630 = 23,789.82 + 9.85%. Divide by periods; 'You may round the amount to the nearest dollar'. No W-4MN = single, zero allowances; W-4MN copies to DOR if >10 allowances or exempt box with wages >200/week; exempt claim renewed yearly. Supplemental 6.25% (Method 1 aggregate / Method 2 flat). Backup withholding 9.85%. Nonresidents: no MN withholding if expected pay < 15,300 or MI/ND reciprocity with MWR. Deposits on the federal semiweekly/monthly schedule (monthly by the 15th), MN did not adopt the one-day rule; quarterly returns Apr 30/Jul 31/Oct 31/Jan 31, filed electronically; annual filers (<=500 prior year) Jan 31. W-2 to employees and W-2 information to DOR by Jan 31; e-Services mandatory if more than 10 W-2 + 1099. Withholding definitions follow the IRC as amended through 2023-05-01; MN has not adopted the H.R. 1 (2025) withholding changes. 2026 interest rate 7%.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.9445-181.9448 Earned Sick and Safe Time (ESST)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 1+ employees; employee = anticipated to work 80+ hours/year in MN (temporary and part-time included). Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked, max 48 hours/year unless the employer agrees more; carryover with an 80-hour balance cap, or front-load 48 h (if unused hours are paid out at year end) / 80 h (if not paid out); FLSA 213(a)(1) exempt employees deemed to work 40 h/week; accrual from hire; use as accrued, increments not below 15 min nor required above 4 h. At the end of each pay period the employer must provide, in writing or electronically, the ESST hours available and the hours used in the period (on or attached to the earnings statement or via an electronic system). No payout at separation required (181.9448 subd. 2). Benefits maintained; return at the same rate. Last amended 1Sp2025 c 6 art 5.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.79 (deductions for loss/indebtedness) and 181.06 (assignment of wages; payroll deductions)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction for lost/stolen property, damage or any employee debt unless the employee authorises it in writing after the loss/debt arises (amount per pay period stated) or a court holds the employee liable; never above the garnishment-exempt limit; exceptions: CBA, commissioned-salespeople rules, prior written authorisation for a purchase/loan from the employer. Violation: liable for twice the deduction. 181.06: assignment of wages earned more than 60 days ahead void (except above the first 1,500/month for less than 5 years); a written contract may authorise deductions for union dues, insurance premiums, credit unions, charities, PACs, ESPP/savings plans and similar.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 571.922 Limitation on wage garnishment
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-support garnishment: the lesser of the tiered percentage of disposable earnings (25% if weekly income > 80x the hourly minimum; 15% if > 60x and <= 80x; 10% if > 40x and <= 60x) or the excess of disposable earnings over 40x the greater of the state minimum wage (177.24 subd. 1(a)(4)) or the federal minimum, per work week in the pay period. Child-support judgments: 50%/55% (supporting a spouse/child, judgment <=12 / >12 weeks old) or 60%/65% (not supporting). Stricter than CCPA 25%. Last amended 1Sp2025 c 4 art 7 s 34.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 518A.53 Income withholding (child support)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payor remits withheld support to the public authority within 7 business days of the payday, with the obligor's SSN; no discharge/discipline because of withholding; multiple orders honoured within CCPA 15 USC 1673(b) limits with priority to current support; termination of employment notified to the public authority within 10 days (home address, new payor if known). Support withholding has priority over any other attachment, execution, garnishment or wage assignment (subd. 9), which lists the employer's fee for processing a withholding notice; the fee amount was not located in the text read. Income-withholding-only service fee 15 USD/month charged to the obligor.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.044 Wage reporting (UI quarterly wage detail report)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly wage detail report by electronic transmission in the commissioner's format: per employee name, SSN, total wages and total paid hours worked (exempt full-time employees: 40 h per week with duties; reasonable estimate otherwise); wages may be reported to the next lower whole dollar; a report is required each quarter even with no wages until termination of business is notified. Late fee 10 USD per employee (minimum 250), doubled if not filed 30 days after demand; missing/erroneous data 25 USD per employee; omitted employee 2% of that employee's wages. Quarterly due date not stated in this section.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 142A.29 Work reporting system (new-hire reporting; renumbered from 256.998)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Report each new hire or rehire (return after 60+ days' separation) of an employee who resides or works in MN, within 20 calendar days of the date of hiring, to the Commissioner of Children, Youth, and Families; not required if employed less than 2 months and gross under 250 USD/month; contents = federal requirements; means: copy of W-4/W-9, electronic media or other authorised means; domestic service in a private home excluded from 'employee'; the state and political subdivisions must also report independent contractors, other payors may. Penalty 25 USD per intentionally unreported employee after a notice of noncompliance.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.035 subd. 20 (noncovered employment) and subd. 24 (taxable wages)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wages = wages in covered employment per calendar year up to 60% of the state's average annual wage, rounded to the nearest 1,000 (2026 figure 44,000 in US-MN-P5-2-001). Not covered: churches, church-controlled religious nonprofits and church schools; ministers and members of religious orders; domestic employment if quarterly domestic wages were under 1,000 in the current and prior year; employment by a son/daughter/spouse and of a child under 18 by a parent; students employed by their school; full-time students in credit programmes; J-1 summer work travel; Minneapolis/St. Paul student interns; student nurses; casual non-business employment; agricultural employment unless 'covered agricultural employment' (subd. 11, not read); H-2A workers. Read literally; replaces the summarizer reading in US-MN-P5-1-003.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268B.14 Paid Leave premiums (statute text)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payments by electronic payment (also third-party processors). Employer pays at least 50% of the premium; the employee share is a wage deduction in equal proportion to wages and may not reduce pay below the minimum wage. Wage cap = maximum earnings subject to OASDI in the year. Statutory base rates from 2026-01-01: 0.7% (family + medical), 0.4% (medical only, private family plan), 0.3% (family only, private medical plan); the commissioner may adjust before 2026-01-01 and must adjust by July 31 each year for the following year (projected fund balance >= 25%). The adjusted rate in force (0.88% for 2026 and 2027) is on the DEED page, US-MN-P5-2-003. History ends 1Sp2025 c 6 art 4 s 27. Replaces the summarizer reading US-MN-P5-1-002.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 325E.59 Use of Social Security numbers
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Private persons may not publicly display an SSN, require its transmission over the Internet unless secure/encrypted, require it to access a website without a password, or print it on materials mailed to the individual unless state or federal law requires it (mailed applications/forms allowed); exceptions for uses required/authorised by law and internal verification/administrative use. No statutory SSN-truncation rule for pay statements located (the 181.032 content list does not require the SSN).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.30 Keeping records (MFLSA)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payroll records kept for three years in the premises where the employee works; employers on state-funded public works projects keep them three years after the project (177.41-177.44).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.068 Notice to workers (UI)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Posting duty only: the employer posts the DEED-supplied statement of the right to apply for unemployment benefits. No individual UI separation notice in statute (the 2020 executive-order notice expired 2020-12-31; tier-B lead only).

instrument_name: Laws 2026, chapter 106 (H.F. 4074), article 15 (retirement omnibus; firefighter conforming changes)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: The only 2026 session-law amendment found in the payroll statutes read this pass: 181.101 amended by art. 15 s 5 (volunteer/paid on-call firefighter terminology); no change to the 31-day rule. The history notes of 177.24, 177.25, 181.13, 181.14, 268.044, 268B.14, 181.9446-.9448 and 571.922 carry no 2026 chapter (latest 1Sp2025).
